_comment: Expectations for `make ext_call_inventory_selftest`.
Each `form_*.ail` uses one of the four indirection forms ADR-001 D5 names as
outside classifier 2's matcher boundary. Every one MUST be reported unresolved.
A fixture that comes back clean is not a pass -- it is the fail-open defect the
classifier exists to prevent, and the suite treats silence as failure.
`control_resolved.ail` must come back with one RESOLVED site and nothing
unresolved. Without it a classifier that flagged everything would pass.
`membership` records the set derived from D5's criterion at this revision. It
is a regression guard, NOT the classifier's input: the tool re-derives
membership from ExtPorts, Ports and the bridge on every run and never reads
this file. Widening the ABI in Milestone B is expected to change these values,
and the self-test going red is how that change gets noticed rather than
absorbed.
WI-B4 added `seam` beside `state`, and it is the BRIDGE's positive control.
`control_resolved.ail` proves the call-site matcher still works; nothing
proved that `bridge_map` still follows `ext_ports_of` down to a core `Ports`
field. That half fails OPEN -- a parsing slip returns `unrouted` for
everything, which reads like a clean result while meaning the field has left
the gated set entirely. WI-B2b hit it twice in one item. Pinning the state
alone would also miss a slip that resolved a field to the WRONG seam, so the
seam is pinned too. `"seam": null` is correct ONLY for a genuinely unrouted
field, and AT HEAD THERE IS NO SUCH FIELD. `clock_now` was the one example
until WI-C5 widened ExtPorts.clock_now to (ExtWorld) -> ExtClockReading and
routed it through Ports.clock_now, so it derives `returns-it` like ai_step.
The `null` seam is kept described here because the next un-widened seam
re-introduces it, and because a pin whose only legal value is unreachable is
worth naming as such rather than deleting.
WI-D16 MOVED THIS BLOCK DELIBERATELY, and the move is the item's point rather
than a cost of it. `tool_handle` was widened from `(string, string) -> string` to
`(ExtWorld, string, string) -> ExtProcOutcome`, so it can now return the
successor `Ports.tool_exec` threads. D5's classifier 2 selects a field
BECAUSE it cannot return successor state; the field can, so the criterion no
longer selects it and the set went {env_get, tool_handle} -> {env_get}. It moved
member -> returns-it, which is the same transition WI-B2b made for `ai_step`
and WI-C5 for `clock_now`, and the seam was then unchanged at Ports.tool_exec.
WI-D24 MOVED THE SEAM, AND THIS PIN IS WHY THE MOVE IS RECORDED RATHER THAN
NOTICED. `tool_handle` now derives Ports.ext_effect_exec, not Ports.tool_exec.
The state is unchanged at `returns-it`; what changed is WHICH core seam the
bridge closure forwards to, because an extension-initiated dispatch is a
different D2 identity class from a driver tool call, is served from a
different cursor (WorldState.ext_effects) and is recorded by a different
adapter (ports.recording_ext_effect, the eighth). This is exactly the slip
the seam half of this pin was added to catch -- the state pin alone would
have stayed green through a re-route -- so it fired as designed and is
re-recorded here with the reason rather than relaxed.
`env_get` is the SOLE remaining member and was left un-widened on purpose --
see its row in packages/motoko-ext-abi/types.ail. Its problematic callers are
in `register_with_config`, which runs before a world exists and has no
`ExtCtx`, so a wider seam would route nothing.
`file_read` is NEW at WI-D16 and derives `returns-it` off Ports.file_read. It
has ZERO call sites: the item shipped the seam and routed no extension.
`file_write` and `file_remove` are NEW at WI-D17 and derive `returns-it` off
Ports.file_write and Ports.file_remove. Zero call sites, same as file_read --
part 2 is what routes compose. The ORDER matters and is the reason WI-D16 did
not add them: a field fronting no core seam derives `unrouted`, which is
derive.py's fail-open answer and looks like a cleaner result than it is. The
core world class landed first, so these two derive `returns-it` instead.
AND THE SUITE COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THE ADDITION. The membership loop iterates
THIS BLOCK, so a field added to ExtPorts and not added here was simply never
asked about -- four green pinned rows and total silence on the fifth. WI-D16
added a REACHABILITY assertion in derive.py that compares the derived field set
against this block in both directions, on plan rule S24: reachability is a
separate question from any verdict and has to be asserted separately.
THAT ASSERTION EARNED ITSELF AT WI-D17, ON THE FIRST ADDITION AFTER IT LANDED.
Adding file_write and file_remove produced, before this block was edited:
FAIL REACHABILITY: ExtPorts.file_remove derives 'returns-it' but is not
pinned in expected.json. A new ABI row is not covered by a pin that does
not name it.
-- two named failures where the pre-D16 suite would have printed five green
membership rows and said nothing at all about the two new fields.
AND IT EARNED ITSELF AGAIN AT WI-D18, WHICH IS THE POINT WORTH RECORDING.
The directory class added path_stat, dir_list and dir_make; all three derived
`returns-it` off their new core seams and all three failed by name before this
block was edited. Three items in a row, three additions, three named failures
-- the assertion is now the only thing in this tool that notices an ABI row
arriving, and the membership loop below still cannot.
8.0 (031 PLAN-001 P1.7r, ADR-001 D2/D7 'the leaf inventory must recognize every view type as a
receiver'). Three things taught, each with a control and a negative, each a one-line rule in derive.py:
* VIEWS: a record every field of which is an ExtPorts field with the IDENTICAL signature is a view
(the ABI's FsPorts/AiPorts/InterceptPorts; an extension's own narrower record). Derived by
STRUCTURE every run and pinned below in `port_views` in both directions, like `membership`. A call
through a view is a resolved call (control_view_receiver).
* PROJECTIONS: an ExtPorts field taken as a value is resolved when it is the same-named field of a
record literal in a function whose declared result type is a view declaring it -- the ABI's
fs_ports/ai_ports/intercept_ports, 15 sites that read as form 3 and made every closure UNRESOLVED.
Counted as `projections`, never as calls (control_view_projection); any other value-escape is
still form 3 (form_projection_not_a_view).
* SCOPED BINDERS: a parameter's type is read from ITS function, not from the first declaration of
that name in the file (control_scoped_binder: agentcli's `p: Provider`, compose's `ctx: PureCtx`).
RE-PIN, NAMED: `form_alias.ail` 1 unresolved -> 1 resolved. Scoping the binders exposed that every
in-tree `let p = ctx.ports` (herdr x4, compose x2; 31 call sites) had been counted resolved only
through some OTHER function's `p: ExtPorts`. The sharpened rule binds an alias of a DECLARED-typed
path to the type that path resolves to in scope -- the same declaration-only lookup a direct
`ctx.ports.ai_step(` gets, one step earlier, no inference; 009 ADR-001 D5 names the alias as a
limit of the grep approximation, not as a rule, and asks for the type-aware form. The alias of an
UNDECLARED source is what form 1 still means: form_alias_untyped.ail keeps it unresolved.

form_alias.ail.form: RE-PINNED 8.0 (P1.7r): alias of a DECLARED-typed path resolves in scope, no inference

form_wrapper.ail.form: wrapper (field escapes as a value, call site elsewhere)

form_computed.ail.form: computed receiver (shares form 2's detector on this pin)

form_alias_untyped.ail.form: form 1 as it survives: alias of an UNDECLARED source stays unresolved

control_view_receiver.ail.form: 8.0 control: calls through AiPorts / FsPorts views resolve

control_view_projection.ail.form: 8.0 control: same-named projection into a (local) view, then a call through it

form_projection_not_a_view.ail.form: form 3 still: forwarded under another name / into a non-view record

control_scoped_binder.ail.form: 8.0 control: binders read from THEIR function (first `p`/`ctx` in the file are not ports)

_comment: The ABI's views of ExtPorts, derived by structure every run (never read from here), pinned
by name and field set in BOTH directions: a view the ABI adds without a pin is a receiver
nobody reviewed; a pinned view that stops deriving is a projection the ABI dropped or a
signature that drifted from ExtPorts, which would silently turn every call through it back
into form 3. Extension-local views (compose's SnippetExecPorts, RemovePorts) are reported
by the inventory and not pinned here: they belong to their package.
